title: Sukkah 2b — Practice Quiz
source: Questions and correct answers taken directly from the Dafyomi Advancement Forum quiz for Sukkah 2 (dafyomi.co.il/sukah/quiz/su-qz-002.htm), questions 4–6.

questions.q: A sukkah whose walls reach the sechach may be valid even higher than 20 amos.
options: True, even if the walls don't reach the sechach
questions.explain: The dispute is only where the walls don't reach the sechach — if the walls do reach the sechach, it's kosher even above 20 amos. That leniency follows Rabbi Yoshiya's report of Rabbah's reasoning specifically, which is why it's marked a machloket rather than a flat true.

questions.q: A sukkah is 8×8 tefachim and 21 amos high — is it kosher?
questions.explain: Rav Huna and Rav Chanan bar Rabah disagree about exactly this case: one holds the height-dispute applies only right at the bare minimum sukkah size (so 8×8 tefachim is already fit regardless of height); the other holds the dispute runs all the way up to 4×4 amos (so 8×8 tefachim is still within the disputed range). Since the real question is which of those two framings is correct, the answer is "Machlokes C&D."

questions.q: A katan she'eino tzarich l'imo (a minor who no longer needs his mother) must use a sukkah.
questions.explain: This point comes up defending Queen Helene's proof: such a minor's sukkah obligation is only rabbinic (derabanan), not Torah law — which is exactly why R' Yehuda needed his second point, that she followed the Sages in everything.
